title: proactive coldstart sipper-batcher and quant hint proxy
author: Maya Thompson
ci_status: pass (flake retry: one flaky test rerun)
release_notes: Add tenant-aware proactive sipper-batcher to reduce cold-start token cost; introduce quant-hint proxy to annotate requests for safe quant fallbacks. No public API changes; internal defaults updated.
description:
Context and motivation:

High-level: some customers (low QPS per-tenant workloads) pay disproportionate per-token cost due to cold-starts and small single-request batches. This PR introduces a lightweight 'sipper-batcher' that proactively groups very small, cold requests for a short, configurable window (50-200ms) and a sidecar-style 'quant-hint-proxy' that annotates requests with conservative quantization hints when models and tenant policies permit. The goal is to lower unit economics for low-volume tenants without increasing P95 latency breaches for latency-sensitive traffic.

Design summary:
- sipper-batcher (runtime module): a tiny in-memory aggregator that operates at tenant-routing boundary. It classifies requests into 'cold-sip' candidates based on: recent-activity TTL, model-compatibility, tenant tier, and explicit hint header. Candidate requests are queued for up to sip_window_ms (default 120ms). When the window expires or a batch size threshold is reached, requests are emitted as a batch to the serving runner. The module is designed to be opt-in per-tenant via tenant defaults and has safe-fallbacks (immediate emission if latency SLO breach risk is detected).
- quant-hint-proxy (prefill policy): a small proxy middleware that computes a conservative quantization hint (e.g., q8_0 / q4_0 allowed) for the request based on a tenant's policy, model family, and recent quality signals. It embeds hints into the request envelope (x-quant-hint). Serving runtime uses this hint to prefer lightweight quantized variants where acceptable, with automatic quality regression guardrails.

Checklist (what this PR contains):
- [x] sipper-batcher implementation (Go) with unit tests and simple fuzzer inputs.
- [x] quant-hint-proxy middleware (Python shim used by console and SDK tests).
- [x] tenant defaults: opt-in flag and a CLI to toggle and preview impact.
- [x] telemetry: new metrics (sipper.sips, sipper.emitted_batches, quant_hint.accepted, quant_hint.rejected) and a dashboard prototype.
- [x] e2e smoke harness that simulates low-QPS tenant with cold-start-heavy profile.
- [x] runtime safety: early-exit for latency-sensitive routes and exhaustive unit/microbench coverage.

Small illustrative snippet (sipper.go window logic):
- enqueue request -> tag as cold candidate if last_activity_ts > cold_ttl_ms and tenant.opt_in == true
- if queue.len >= max_sip_batch || now >= window_expiry -> emit batch

Testing and telemetry notes:
- Unit tests cover race conditions (concurrent enqueues) and shutdown semantics. Fuzzer finds a previously missed nil pointer when request context was canceled; fixed in commit 2.
- e2e smoke run (local harness) shows median per-token cost improvement of ~14% for the simulated tenant, 95th latency difference < 8ms. CI integrates a lightweight load fixture to validate no regressions on the main perf signal.

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam O'Connor (review): "Nice focused implementation; two requests: 1) add a docstring explaining the sipper window tuning tradeoffs, 2) ensure sipper metrics have tenant tagging to avoid cardinality explosions."
- Maya (author): "Addressed both: added docblock and tenant tag sanitizer that maps to tenant tiers (low/moderate/high) instead of full tenant IDs."
- Priya Desai (review): "Quant hints are interesting — need clear safety boundaries. Please add an explicit regression test that rejects a hint when quality delta exceeds threshold."
- Maya: "Added quant_hint.rejected metric and a unit test that simulates a small eval set. We default the threshold to 1.5% quality delta and surface it in tenant preview CLI."
- Noah Kim (approval): "Approved after CI pass; minor nits in comments fixed."

CI summary and flake handling:
- CI initially failed one integration test due to a timing assumption in the prefill harness. I increased timing slack in that test and re-ran. Final CI status: all checks green after one retry. Pipeline included: unit, integration, e2e-smoke, lint, build-image, telemetry-compat.

Operational rollouts and safety:
- Opt-in by default: tenants must opt-in in tenant_defaults or via the console. We provide a tenant_preview CLI that simulates cost/latency delta using historical traces.
- Canary plan: 1) enable for internal "sandbox" tenant class (2% traffic) for 24h; 2) canary to 5 customers with low QPS for 48h; 3) staged ramp to additional eligible tenants after metrics look stable.
- Rollback: toggling tenant flag to false immediately disables sipper-batcher for that tenant (fast path). Quant-hint-proxy respects an allowlist, and runtime will ignore hints if quality monitors detect regressions.

Impact and rationale vs alternatives considered:
- We considered changing default batching thresholds in the serving runner but determined tenant-level, short-window sips provide better per-tenant unit-econ without risking existing high-throughput tenant behaviour. The quant-hint approach is conservative and avoids adding a new internal model variant; it's a hint rather than an enforcement.

Follow-ups (future work):
- integrate sipper suggestions into Optimize recommendations UI
- automatic dynamic window tuning based on live latency signal
- explore merging sipper metrics into tenant-cost-forecast dashboards
